_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For tactical-rmm the manifest gained: TACTICAL_RMM_BASE_URL. server.json gained: TACTICAL_RMM_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: TACTICAL_RMM_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 12 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: agents meshcentral agents-agents (POST /agents/{agent_id}/meshcentral/); agents reboot agents-agents (POST /agents/{agent_id}/reboot/); agents shutdown agents (POST /agents/{agent_id}/shutdown/); alerts alerts-bulk (POST /alerts/bulk/); autotasks run autotasks (POST /autotasks/{pk}/run/); checks reset checks (POST /checks/{pk}/reset/); checks resetall checks (POST /checks/{agent_id}/resetall/); scripts test scripts (POST /scripts/{agent_id}/test/); services services-agentid-2 (POST /services/{agent_id}/{svcname}/); software software-agentid-2 (POST /software/{agent_id}/); software uninstall software (POST /software/{agent_id}/uninstall/); winupdate install winupdate (POST /winupdate/{agent_id}/install/).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: Every mirrored MCP tool that can change Tactical RMM data (agents bulk-run and maintenance set via --execute, import, services down) previews and sends only with boolean confirm: true
handfixes.why: Press 4.35.1 confirm-gates only the code-orchestration execute tool. The mirrored novels agents_bulk_run ({"execute": true, "command": ...} ran a command on every matched agent) and maintenance_set (PUT maintenance mode on a cohort) and the framework import tool sent without confirm. internal/mcp/cobratree/trmm_confirm.go (wired in generated internal/mcp/tools.go after RegisterAll; any mcp-sync or tools.go regeneration drops the call) runs a command annotated mcp:read-only-unless-flags without those flags unless confirm is boolean true, and previews every other non-read-only, non-local mirrored tool with the root --dry-run forced on, so the mirror's own argument checks still refuse blocked flags by name (check_mcp_file_flags). Tests fail if the wiring or an annotation is lost.

handfixes.summary: Vendor GETs that act (bulkrecovery, clearcache) or dispatch to the managed agent (ping, processes, eventlog, registry, services) are spec mutations: no sync, export, tail or local read calls them, and over MCP they need confirm
handfixes.why: amidaware/tacticalrmm GET /agents/bulkrecovery/ queues bulk_recover_agents_task and GET /core/clearcache/ runs clear_entire_cache; the reconstructed spec modelled both as array GETs, so the press made them list endpoints and a plain sync (also the MCP sync tool), export core, tail and workflow archive fired them (published 0.1.7). GET ping/processes/eventlog/registry/services dispatch nats commands to the endpoint (services also saves agent.services). Spec repair in the library spec.json (x-pp-mutation, bulkrecovery/clearcache answer {type: string}; survives a reprint from that spec); generated resourceDetailPaths must not map them (bin/reapply_detail_paths.py); services down is not mcp:read-only. TestActionGETsAreNeverReadPaths walks the tree and fails on any read path to such a GET. Generated client.go doInternal calls refuseReadOfActionRoute (internal/client/trmm_action_routes.go; re-apply bin/reapply_action_guard.py): a plain Get whose percent-decoded, dot-cleaned path routes to one of these is refused, so an id (export agents bulkrecovery) or an encoded slash (read agents/<id>%2Fping) cannot reach them; GetMutating, the action commands' own call, may.

handfixes.summary: sync also stores the alert list (PATCH /alerts/ with an empty body) as resource type alerts-list; the alert reports read it and count an alert active only when resolved and snoozed are both false
handfixes.why: The generated sync walks GET lists only, so its alerts partition is GET /alerts/templates/ (alert TEMPLATES); fleet health, alerts digest, clients scorecard and since read those rows as alerts (published 0.1.7: every template counted as an active alert). vendor-src/alerts/views.py GetAddAlerts.patch is the alert list; its dashboard count excludes resolved and snoozed. internal/cli/trmm_alerts_sync.go wraps sync through registerNovelCommand (no generated-file edit), replaces the stored list, and fails on an answer that is not an array of alerts with ids. TestAlertReportsReadTheAlertList runs the real sync against a fake server.

handfixes.why: The shared cohort parser dropped unknown keys and malformed entries, so `maintenance set --filter client_name=Acme --execute` (a typo for client) put every synced agent into maintenance (Codex review 2026-11-02). novelAgentFilterWhere now returns a usage error; with no filter the cohort is empty unless --all. TestCohortWritesRefuseFiltersTheyCannotApply drives both commands against a fake server and counts writes.

handfixes.summary: clients scorecard has a row for every synced client and fleet health counts sites from the synced site list, not from agents
handfixes.why: Rows came from agents only, so a client or site with no agents vanished and same-named sites in different clients collapsed (Codex review 2026-11-02; vendor-src/clients/views.py GetAddClients.get, GetAddSites.get). TestReportsCountClientsAndSitesFromTheirOwnLists.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand: internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one credkit.Declarations literal, both mains start with credkit.Start(credwire.Declarations) and end with credkit.Exit, every HTTP client (API, --deliver webhook and Spacefast, feedback, probe) goes through credkit.Transport, every SQLite handle through the credkit.SQLDriver internal/credsql registers, every program file write through the kit, child processes through credkit.RunCommand, and the MCP stdio and HTTP servers through credkit.MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP. The credential store, config and the Spacefast delivery record are sources, written outside the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile). A saved profile's base-url (current and legacy store, any spelling, every duplicate) is held through credkit.HoldURL as profile:base-url, sent nowhere; a newly issued Spacefast page key is held the moment the publish returns, and the key-bearing door URL is never printed.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector's own layer. It retires secret-echo-decoded-funnel (replaced by the shared credential kit; the 4.35.1 reprint had already dropped its files). Classes closed, each by a test seen failing first on the pre-kit build (.review/leak-tests-seen-failing-prekit.log): an API error that echoes part of TRMM_API_KEY (TestAPIErrorEchoOfKeyIsWithheld, CLI, --agent and MCP); the key in config.toml, a malformed config, auth_header, a [headers] table and the 0600 store held at startup (TestConfigKeyHeldAtStartup); the key refused to another origin and over plain http (TestHeldCredentialRefusedOffOriginAndOverPlainHTTP); SPACEFAST_TOKEN held (TestSpacefastTokenHeld); the learn journal, written with credkit.AppendFile, never records a held credential (TestJournalNeverRecordsAHeldCredential), which closes the journal class; feedback --stdin keeps its body and a pasted key never reaches feedback.jsonl (TestFeedbackStdinIsRecorded). Regression guards: auth set-token's piped key is held as read (TestSetTokenFromStdinIsNeverPrinted) and mirrored MCP tools' CLI child still authenticates through the kit (TestMCPShellOutChildAuthenticates). In-process tests never run Start, so cliutil.OutboundGuard, Hold and HoldBody are variables the test mains swap (root_test.go, credkit_seam_test.go). The MCP sql value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to the _length_limit DSN parameter, and openReadOnlySQLite runs select 1 because the kit's connection does not forward Ping. The action-route guard line in client.go doInternal is kept.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal and one kit-wrapped SQLite driver name.

handfixes.summary: checks worst and checks flapping --snapshot read each agent's check status live from GET /agents/{agent_id}/checks/ (check_result.status); the synced GET /checks/ list carries no status; checks worst scans every agent with a failing check of any alert severity (checks.failing, warning or info), since ping, service and event-log checks default to warning
handfixes.why: Tactical RMM keeps a check's status on the per-agent CheckResult (vendor-src/checks/views.py GetAddChecks.get); GET /checks/ is CheckSerializer over Check rows with check_result {}. checks worst grouped '$.status' over the synced checks and printed [] on every real fleet while fleet health reported failing checks (executed repro .review/adv/t10.sh), and checks flapping --snapshot stored an empty status for every check. internal/cli/checks_live.go fans out to the failing agents (capped by --max-scan-agents); a check with no result is unknown, a fetch failure is never an empty result. TestChecksWorstRanksPerAgentCheckResults, TestChecksWorstFetchFailuresAreNotEmptyResults, TestChecksFlappingSnapshotRecordsPerAgentStatus.

handfixes.summary: patch posture --by site keys each row on (client, site) and names the client; agents bulk-run and maintenance set refuse a --filter site= name that more than one client uses unless client= picks one
handfixes.why: Site names are unique only within a client (vendor-src/clients/views.py GetAddSites), so two clients each with a site called Main is ordinary MSP data. patch posture grouped on site_name alone and merged both Main sites into one row (executed repro .review/adv/t11.sh: one row of 4 agents for Acme/Main and Beta Corp/Main), and the cohort selector matched site_name alone, so maintenance set --filter site=Main --execute toggled agents in both clients. internal/cli/trmm_site_identity.go holds the rule: the site id when the agent row carries one (GET /agents/{agent_id}/ rows), resolved through the synced site list, else (client, site name). TestPatchPostureBySiteKeepsSameNamedSitesApart, TestPatchPostureBySitePrefersTheSiteIDOnDetailRows, TestCohortSiteFilterNeedsClientWhenTheNameRepeats.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template's per-page progress line should be throttled, as its dependent walk already is (not filed yet).

retired.reason: tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
